title: HardFault with INVSTATE after calling callback
serial_logs:
HardFault!
CFSR = 0x00020000 (UFSR.INVSTATE)  HFSR = 0x40000000 (FORCED)
PC   = 0x00000000  LR = 0x08000a3b
MMFAR: not valid (CFSR.MMARVALID=0)  BFAR: not valid (CFSR.BFARVALID=0)
user_question: Happens on first received byte. uart_register_cb() is only called in some build configs.

reference_context.title: Cortex-M4 Devices Generic User Guide (Arm)
reference_context.section: 4.3.10 Configurable Fault Status Register > UsageFault Status Register, Table 4-27 UFSR bit assignments
reference_context.snippet: [1] INVSTATE Invalid state UsageFault: 0 = no invalid state UsageFault 1 = the processor has attempted to execute an instruction that makes illegal use of the EPSR. When this bit is set to 1, the PC value stacked for the exception return points to the instruction that attempted the illegal use of the EPSR.

reference_context.title: Cortex-M4 Devices Generic User Guide (Arm)
reference_context.section: 4.3.11 HardFault Status Register, Table 4-28 HFSR bit assignments
reference_context.snippet: [30] FORCED Indicates a forced hard fault, generated by escalation of a fault with configurable priority that cannot be handles, either because of priority or because it is disabled: 0 = no forced HardFault 1 = forced HardFault. When this bit is set to 1, the HardFault handler must read the other fault status registers to find the cause of the fault.

expected.root_cause: on_rx is still NULL; calling it branches to 0x00000000 with the Thumb bit clear, raising a UsageFault INVSTATE that escalates to HardFault.
expected.fix: Check on_rx != NULL before calling it, or give it a default no-op handler.
